chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, or from someone else, from Abu Dawood al-Mustarriq, who said:

Whoever has a flute struck (played) in his house for forty days, Allah will cause a devil called Al-Qafandar to overcome him, so he will not leave any limb of his body parts except that he (the devil) will sit upon it. So when it is like that, modesty will be removed from him, and he will not care what he says, nor what is said about him.

key_terms.الْقَفَنْدَرُ: Al-Qafandar (a specific devil mentioned in the narration)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual effect of playing music in the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi*, this hadith links the domestic practice of playing the flute to a specific spiritual decay, where the devil Al-Qafandar occupies the body for forty days. This prolonged exposure erodes *hayaa'* (modesty), leading to a loss of self-restraint and indifference to social reputation, a concept deeply explored in Shia jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of *lahw* (frivolous) music. The narrative underscores the belief that musical instruments can serve as vessels for spiritual influence, altering the believer's psychological and moral state.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from someone else, from Abu Dawood Al Mustaraq,

(He<sup>asws</sup>): ‘The one who strikes a flute in his house for forty days, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Cause a devil called Al-Qafandar to overcome him, so there would not remain a part from his body parts except that he (the devil) would sit upon it. So when it would be like that, the shame would be removed from him, and he would not care what he says, nor what is said in it’.
en.sarwar: 17. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa or others from abu Dawud al-Mustariq who has said the following:

“He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If barbat is played in one’s house for forty days Allah gives its control to a Satan called al-Qafandar who sits on every part of the body of the owner of the house. When this happens bashfulness (the sense to feel ashamed of one’s indecent acts) is taken away from him and he does not mind whatever he says or is said about him.’”
